summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with critical aortic stenosis, severe diastolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted after two falls and found to be hypotensive with severe anemia (hemoglobin 4.4 g/dL) due to a gastrointestinal bleed. He was transfused three units of packed red blood cells and stabilized. Evaluation revealed a positive H. pylori infection, and he was treated with quadruple therapy. An endoscopy showed gastritis and erosions but no active bleeding source. Due to high bleeding risk, warfarin was discontinued and replaced with aspirin. He developed transient acute kidney injury and mild pulmonary edema, both of which resolved with careful diuresis management. A left olecranon fracture was managed nonoperatively. He improved steadily, was weaned off oxygen, and transitioned to extended care with stable vital signs and hemoglobin of 9.1 g/dL at discharge.
problems: Closed fracture of olecranon process of ulna
Severe chronic diastolic congestive heart failure
